# Piṇḍapātika Sutta (Ud 3.8 (PTS Ud 30))

**ID:** Ud 3.8 (PTS Ud 30)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Piṇḍapātika Sutta* is the eighth discourse of the third chapter (*Nanda Vagga*) of the *Udāna* (Ud 3.8, PTS Ud 30–31). In this discourse, the Buddha rebukes a group of monks who, having returned from their almsround, engage in frivolous conversation concerning the agreeable and tasty food items encountered while begging. The concluding verse praises the sage who lives unburdened and self-reliant [Levman 2014].

Scholarly discussion of the sutta has focused on the linguistic interpretation of its concluding verse (Ud 30.17–31.20), specifically the term *attabharassa* contrasted with *anaññaposino* ("supporting oneself and no other") [Levman 2014]. Bryan G. Levman notes that the commentary (*Paramatthadīpanī*, Ud-a 202) glosses *anaññaposino* as being free from the obligation of maintaining disciples or others with gathered food (*sissādike... posetuṁ anussukkatāya*), and he analyzes whether the prefix *an-* negates the compound *añña-posin* or modifies *añña* directly as an emphatic reflex for the self [Levman 2014].

 In addition, DharmaNexus records widespread internal formulaic text reuse across the canon, sharing its conversational framing passages primarily with the following *Sippa Sutta* (Ud 3.9), the *Rāja Sutta* (Ud 2.2), and discourses such as MN 123 (*Acchariyaabbhuta Sutta*), DN 14 (*Mahāpadāna Sutta*), and AN 10.50 [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments computed by DharmaNexus match parts of its narrative stock phrases with Sanskrit fragments of the *Mahāvadānasūtra*, the Chinese *Dīrghāgama* (T 1), and Tibetan translations such as the *Brahmajālasūtra* (D 352) [DharmaNexus].
